assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity degradation turns the cell's ubiquitin-proteasome machinery into a programmable drug modality, making formerly undruggable targets addressable. It is a molecular design principle with precise control over recognition and has spread from chemical biology to clinical oncology and immunology.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the bifunctional PROTAC concept; Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explained the molecular-glue mechanism. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others made decisive later contributions, so the three-person cut is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups, extensive structural validation, and degraders now in late-stage clinical trials. Timing is good, though regulatory approval of a bifunctional degrader is still pending (as far as I know).
uncertainties: Which of Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and Sakamoto has the strongest claim is unresolved.
Clinical validation of heterobifunctional degraders is not yet complete (not independently verified).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry that made siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines deliverable, with enormous demonstrated effect on what clinicians can do. The work is applied physical and lipid chemistry with clear originality in the pH-dependent ionizable-lipid design and microfluidic formulation.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden) built the core formulation science; Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan contributed lipid optimization and industrial translation. The credit is spread across academia and industry, and the mRNA biology itself was already recognized in Medicine.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at global scale and independently reproduced; recognition is timely, though the 2023 Medicine prize may make the committee cautious about overlap.
uncertainties: Overlap with the mRNA-vaccine recognition in Medicine may be judged a concern.
Allocation among academic and industrial inventors is difficult, partly due to patent history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs let cells encode noncanonical amino acids, giving chemists site-specific control over protein composition in living organisms. This is a clear, original molecular tool with broad use in biophysics, biosensing, biotherapeutics and materials.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first in vivo expansion in E. coli and eukaryotes; Chin extended it to quadruplet codons, multiple codes and engineered ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama also made contributions, so an alternative trio is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Mature: widely adopted for two decades, with therapeutic proteins (antibody-drug conjugates) in development.
uncertainties: Whether Chin or Wang is the third laureate is uncertain.
Several parts of the field (ribosome engineering) are still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed how cells organize biochemistry without membranes and connected polymer physics to cell biology and disease. The concept is original and influential, with implications for neurodegeneration and drug targeting.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated liquid-like P granules; Rosen showed multivalent phase separation from defined components. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical theory and sequence grammar.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly adopted but still debated: the physiological relevance of phase separation versus other assemblies is contested, and the field is arguably still maturing.
uncertainties: Controversy over in vivo relevance and over methods for distinguishing true phase separation.
Whether this is chemistry or physiology/biology for the prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Shokat's covalent targeting of the KRAS G12C switch-II pocket cracked a target long considered undruggable, and his analog-sensitive kinase chemical genetics gave a general tool for dissecting signaling. It is a clean story of chemical design leading to approved medicines.
assessment.attribution: Single credited person with clearly decisive and well-documented contributions; other medicinal-chemistry teams developed the clinical agents but the founding concept is Shokat's.
assessment.maturity: Approved KRAS G12C drugs exist and the chemistry is independently validated; resistance mechanisms are still being studied.
uncertainties: A solo prize may be seen as ignoring industrial development teams.
Single-person attribution may conflict with the committee's wish to recognize a broader field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: DNA-programmed nanoparticle assembly gave rational, sequence-addressable control over nanoparticle architecture, and spherical nucleic acids became both a materials design principle and a biosensing/therapeutic platform. This is close to my own area, which makes me wary of bias.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos independently reported the first DNA-nanoparticle conjugates and assemblies in 1996; Mirkin then led the development of spherical nucleic acids and diagnostics. Storhoff and Mucic were key coauthors but not obvious laureates.
assessment.maturity: Approximately three decades of research and commercial diagnostics; clinical impact of therapeutic spherical nucleic acids is less established.
uncertainties: Alivisatos may be better recognized for quantum dots, complicating a joint prize.
Clinical translation of therapeutic uses remains unproven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Activity-based probes report on enzyme function rather than abundance and enabled proteome-wide functional profiling and inhibitor discovery in native systems. This is a bioanalytical and chemical biology tool with real translational reach.
assessment.attribution: Cravatt developed ABPP and its extension to serine hydrolases and to covalent ligand discovery; Bogyo made major contributions to protease probes and imaging. Overkleeft and Weerapana are also credited, so the proposed pair is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted; covalent chemoproteomics is expanding quickly but its drug-discovery payoff is still emerging.
uncertainties: Whether Overkleeft or Weerapana deserve inclusion.
The tool is widely used, but a single transformative discovery is less crisp.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large-scale and quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics changed what biologists and clinicians can measure about cells and disease, building on earlier ionization prizes. Its impact is across virtually all of the life sciences and clinical biomarker work.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates each introduced decisive strategies (quantitative workflows, targeted/SRM and shotgun proteomics, and data-dependent identification). Hunt, Gygi and Heck also contributed major methods, so credit is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and independently confirmed; the main question is whether the field has already been recognized through the 2002 ESI/MALDI prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize may weigh against it.
Method development is spread across several strong groups.
